statement: A barn has a row of stalls; stalls holds their positions on a line, in sorted order. You have k cows to put in the stalls, at most one cow per stall.
The cows fight when they are close together, so place them to make the smallest distance between any two cows as large as possible.

Return that largest possible minimum distance. For a candidate distance d, placing cows greedily from the leftmost stall, each at the first stall at least d past the previous cow, tells you whether k cows fit. If d works, every smaller distance works too, so binary search for the largest d that works.

examples.explanation: Cows at 1, 4 and 8 are at least 3 apart. A minimum distance of 4 is impossible: after 1 and 8 (or 1 and 9) there is no room for a third cow 4 away.
With only two cows, put them in the two end stalls, 1 and 5, which are 4 apart.
Cows at 0, 3, 7 and 10 are pairwise at least 3 apart. Asking for 4 places cows at 0, 4 and 9 only, one short.
